01

The idea

?edh.wtf asks.

edh.how answers.

The name is the player's question. It is what someone says the first time a precon gets eaten by a turn-four combo, the first time a judge explains color identity, the first time someone at the store says "that's banned". Players say EDH where Wizards' marketing says Commander, so the name is in their words twice.

Nothing else in the house raises its voice. Every page, tool and post answers in plain sentences and shows its work: the card text, the rule number, the count.

How a loud name stays polite

  • The suffix is never expanded or sworn out.Its letters stay in the address and never appear as a word in a sentence.
  • Nothing printed carries it.Goods, labels and packs print edh.how or edh.supply.
  • Every answer shows its work.A tool, guide or community answer that can't show where it came from does not ship.
  • One domain holds everything.edh.how and edh.supply are redirects to paths on edh.wtf, so search authority builds in one place.

Kept from the other candidates

The Tinker story

Jaime's story is the About page and the first email. The community keeps a standing #tinker-stories thread, and the house answers each story with a card to put in the slot instead.

Rule zero

Every deck-box label and every tool that rates a deck carries a bracket line and a plain note on how the deck plays, for the pregame talk.

02

Who it is for, and how it differs

Commander players only. Other games are parked.

Theo, the tinkerer

A dozen decks, brackets 2 and 3. Rebuilds one every few weeks. The primary reader.

Jess

Budget-minded and proxy-curious. Tests cards on paper before she buys them.

Priya, the organizer

Every deck labeled, every box in its place.

Dan

Buys a few precons a year and wants MSRP without the launch-day circus.

The first-month player

Bought a precon, played three games, and has a list of questions and no one to ask who won't roll their eyes.

The job

Commander raises questions no decklist answers. What does color identity actually count? Why does the precon miss its third land drop? Is Tinker banned? (Yes.) Which cards are worth testing on paper before spending $40? The answers exist, scattered across the comprehensive rules, Scryfall rulings, r/EDH threads, EDHREC pages and whatever a chat assistant says with confidence. edh.wtf gathers the answer to each question in one place and shows where it came from.

Swap tests

Each rival is swapped into the full claim: answers to your Commander deck's questions, in words, with the work shown.

  • AI chat assistantsThe real substitute for answers in words. A chat answer cites no rule number a player can check.Closest substitute
  • edh.toolsGives reasons for its card picks, and no LLM is involved. No rules answers, land-count math, guides or supplies.Partial overlap
  • EDHRECRecommends by popularity and synergy: decks like yours run it. Its articles explain; its tools don't explain a rule or a count.Partial overlap
  • TheStack.ggAnswers rules questions for every format, at the table, and teaches new players. It doesn't read your deck, and it isn't Commander-specific.Partial overlap
  • MoxfieldBuilds and playtests lists and flags legality. It answers "is it legal" and nothing else in words.Fails
  • edh.lolKeeps the list, down to the printing. No answers.Fails
  • edh.guideGenerates a 100-card deck from a commander. A list, without reasons.Fails

The one claim only edh.wtf can make

edh.wtf is the only Commander site named for the question players ask, and every answer on it shows its work.

The first half is identity. The second half is a house rule with one live example today: the Mana Base Builder gives a reason and the counts for every land it picks. Until a second tool ships, public copy says no more than that, and it keeps the claim to deck questions.

What edh.wtf is not

  • Not where your list livesedh.lol, Moxfield and Archidekt keep lists. The tools take a paste or an export and give answers back.
  • Not a rulingThe house explains rules and cites them. A judge rules at an event; your pod rules on rule zero.
  • Not a proxy shopProxyPrintr prints playtest cards of your own list for your own table, marked as playtest. EDH Supply sells blank playtest paper, never printed cards.
  • Not an AI deck generatorWe don't generate decks; we explain the one you built.
  • Not WizardsNo mana symbols, card frames or Beleren-like type.

Notices

04

Ask like a player. Answer like the regular.

Principles

  • 01Ask it the way players ask it.Headlines, guide titles and tool prompts use the player's own phrasing, taken from search suggestions and r/EDH thread titles.
  • 02Answer like the regular who has read section 903.Straight and specific. The first sentence is the answer. Name the card, give the number.
  • 03Show the work.Card text quoted, rule cited, count given. If the work is missing, the answer is not finished.CR903.9aCOUNT37 / 100
  • 04Dry is allowed; rude is not.Jokes are the kind regulars make at the pod: about Sol Ring, about salt, about the deck that never draws its third land. Never at the player who asked.
  • 05Explain a term the first time it matters.Brand lines leave players' words unexplained. Guides, tool results, listings, help and errors use the term, then make it plain in the same sentence.
  • 06The name stays in the address.Its last three letters appear only as part of edh.wtf.

Banned

  • Swearing, in any formThe abbreviation is never written as a word, expanded or sworn around. "Find out" never sits next to the name.
  • Hype and scarcityDrop (as a release), only N left, countdown, limited time, insane value, must-have. "Land drop" is fine.
  • Speculator wordsInvestment, ROI, flip, whale.
  • Software-marketing wordsElevate, unlock, unleash, level up, supercharge, seamless, all-in-one, game-changer. The Commander Game Changers list keeps its name.
  • AI in a tool nameNo "AI-powered", and no tool called AI anything.
  • Praise of ourselvesFair, honest, trusted, the best.
  • Emoji, and puns that block a taskNo puns in errors, failed imports or the 404 body. The 404 headline may joke.

Humor itself is not banned.

Explanations, for the first-month player

Guides, tool results, listings, errors and server rules pass the newcomer test: a term is used, then made plain in the same sentence.

?Is Tinker still banned in Commander?

Yes. Tinker is on the Commander banned list, the short list of cards no Commander deck may include. Your pod, the group you play with, can still agree to allow it in a casual game. That agreement is called rule zero, and it's how most house rules work. At a store event, the banned list applies.

LISTCommander banned listORACLETinker

If you want the same idea, legal:

  • 1Transmute ArtifactAlso trades an artifact for one from your library. Legal, and not a Game Changer.U
?How many lands in an EDH deck?

Most decks run 36 to 38 lands. An EDH deck, also called a Commander deck, is 100 cards: your commander plus 99 others, which players call the 99. Run fewer lands if the 99 has plenty of mana rocks, artifacts such as Sol Ring and Arcane Signet that tap for mana. Run more if your best cards cost 6 or more.

COUNT36 to 38SOURCEEDHRECSOURCEDraftsim

About

Jaime upgraded his first deck by hand, with cards he'd kept since he was a kid. He put Tinker in it and thought it was awesome. He and his friends played it for months. Then he took it to his local game store and was told, promptly, that Tinker is banned.

Most Commander players have a story like that. edh.wtf is named for the question that comes right after it. Ask it here and you'll get the answer, the rule behind it, and a card to put in the slot instead: the place in your deck that card held.

08

Mark and wordmarks

The mark is the layout in miniature: the question row over the list. The wordmarks are interim, drawn from the type, until a human letterer redraws them.

5 x 8 units, 0.85 unit frame, split 55 / 45

The house's own screens and the community only.

Guides, and the address printed on goods.

EDH Supply listings and pack fronts.

Minimum sizes

  • Mark on screen, 64 px and upScale the drawn mark freely.
  • Mark below 64 pxUse the pixel fittings at 48, 32, 24 and 16 px, so the frame and the split rule land on whole pixels. 16 px is the smallest.
  • Mark in printAt 5 mm or smaller, use the small-print master, which opens the gap in the question mark. 3.5 mm in 1-bit black is the smallest.
  • WordmarksChecked at 24 px tall on Table. Below that, use the mark alone. On screens the house signs as edh.wtf; anything printed uses edh.how or edh.supply.

Favicon

The favicon is the tall filled key, pixel-fitted at 16, 24, 32 and 48 px and shipped as an SVG that follows the system theme, a multi-size .ico, a 180 px touch icon and a 512 px maskable icon. Keep the key tall: a square key at tab size reads as a help icon.

?Why does this deck want 38 lands?

38 lands. With 38 you make your fourth land drop on time in 58 of 100 games on the play; with 36, in 53.

A land drop is the one land you may play each turn, so your fourth on time means four lands on the table by turn 4.

10

Accessibility

  • Contrast in both themesText at 4.5:1 or better and non-text at 3:1 or better, on every allowed pairing, light and dark.COUNT41 pairings
  • Color is never the only signalKeys carry their letter. A state always carries a word.
  • Faces that separate I, l, 1, O and 0Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Mono, where a column of 1s is the texture and counts are content.
  • Nothing under 12 px on screenTags are the smallest type, at 12 / 16.
  • Focus is always visibleA 2 px Ink outline with a 2 px Marker halo, Mat Text plus Marker in dark. Never removed.
  • Motion only for stateHover, focus and disclosure. Under reduced motion every change is instant.
  • Both themes are designedLight and dark follow the system setting. Neither is an inversion of the other.
  • Grayscale and 1-bit printThe wordmark, the keys and the label must read from a home black-and-white printer at 25 mm.
  • The newcomer testExplanatory copy uses a term, then makes it plain in the same sentence.
  • Wide tables scroll in placeInside their own box, reachable by keyboard, with a visible cue.
